items.assignment: Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining brown Peace Lily leaf tips, how to distinguish tip burn from larger lesions, and how water quality, moisture consistency, humidity, feeding, heat and root condition may contribute. Avoid single-cause diagnosis, fixed watering schedules and unsupported remedies.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining soft or mushy Snake Plant leaves. Cover safe inspection of leaf bases, roots, growing medium, drainage, cold exposure and watering history, with proportionate next steps. Avoid diagnosing root rot from one symptom or promising recovery.

Prepare an evidence-led UK article explaining brown spots on Snake Plant leaves and how readers can compare physical damage, excess moisture, temperature stress, sun exposure and possible pests or disease. Keep diagnosis cautious and avoid unsupported treatments or pesticide recommendations.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to brown tips on Pothos leaves. Cover moisture patterns, roots, feeding, water quality, humidity, heat and physical damage, and explain what readers can inspect before changing care. Avoid assuming low humidity or prescribing rigid routines.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining curled Rubber Plant leaves. Cover new-leaf development, moisture and roots, light, temperature, draughts and pest inspection, with safe corrective priorities. Avoid treating curling as proof of one cause or recommending unsupported sprays.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining a drooping Fiddle Leaf Fig. Cover soil moisture, root condition, recent moves, temperature, light and structural weight, and show how to assess the whole plant before intervening. Avoid fixed watering schedules and guarantees of recovery.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining yellow Calathea leaves. Cover natural ageing, moisture and drainage, roots, light, temperature, feeding and pests, including how to distinguish one ageing leaf from a broader pattern. Avoid overdiagnosis and unsupported water-quality claims.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining drooping or leaning ZZ Plant stems. Cover normal growth habit, light direction, moisture, rhizome and root condition, temperature and physical damage. Distinguish leaning from soft collapse and avoid diagnosing from posture alone.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining soft Aloe vera leaves. Cover hydration, root and crown condition, drainage, cold damage, light and natural lower-leaf ageing, with careful inspection steps. Avoid equating softness automatically with overwatering or recommending unsupported wound treatments.

Prepare an evidence-led UK visual guide to assessing Phalaenopsis orchid roots. Explain how colour can change with moisture, what firmness and tissue condition reveal, how aerial roots differ from pot roots, and when intervention may be justified. Avoid trimming healthy roots or diagnosing by colour alone.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining pale or washed-out Spider Plant leaves. Cover cultivar pattern, light, moisture, roots, feeding, temperature and pest checks, and help readers distinguish gradual paling from local damage. Avoid inventing nutrient deficiencies from appearance alone.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to identifying and managing aphids on indoor plants. Cover identification, cast skins and honeydew, inspection of new growth, isolation and non-chemical first steps, and when UK-authorised products require label-led use. Do not recommend unverified homemade pesticides.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to identifying and managing whiteflies on indoor plants. Cover adults, immature stages, honeydew, underside inspection, isolation, monitoring and safe non-chemical measures. Avoid unsupported pesticide advice and distinguish whiteflies from fungus gnats and other small insects.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining springtails in houseplant compost, how to distinguish them from common pests, what their presence may indicate about moisture and organic matter, and when action is proportionate. Avoid portraying all soil organisms as harmful or prescribing pesticides unnecessarily.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to recognising and responding to cold damage on houseplants. Cover cold windows, draughts, transport exposure, chilled roots and delayed symptoms, with safe stabilisation and pruning guidance. Avoid exact universal temperature thresholds or guarantees of recovery.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide for acclimatising a newly purchased houseplant. Cover quarantine and pest inspection, light transition, moisture assessment, temperature stability, when not to repot immediately and what changes to monitor. Avoid rigid timelines and unnecessary treatments.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to cleaning houseplant leaves safely. Cover when dust removal is useful, support for delicate leaves, suitable water and cloth methods, plants with hairy or fragile foliage, and why oils and leaf-shine products may be inappropriate. Avoid claims that cleaning cures plant problems.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining when and how to inspect houseplant roots without reflexively repotting. Cover external clues, careful removal, root texture and smell, container condition, when to return the plant unchanged and when intervention is justified. Avoid diagnosing from root colour alone.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to dividing a mature Peace Lily. Explain when division may be appropriate, how to identify separate crowns, minimise root disturbance, choose containers and provide aftercare. Avoid fixed division schedules, guarantees of success and unsupported treatments.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining curled or folded Snake Plant leaves. Cover normal leaf form, moisture and roots, temperature, light, physical damage and pests, with safe inspection priorities. Avoid diagnosing solely from curl shape or prescribing unsupported remedies.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining curled Spider Plant leaves. Cover moisture consistency, roots, light, temperature, humidity, feeding and pests, and help readers compare new growth with established leaves. Avoid rigid watering schedules and single-cause claims.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining long gaps and sparse growth on Pothos vines. Cover light, seasonal growth, pruning, support, propagation choices and realistic recovery expectations. Avoid promising that one intervention will restore old bare sections or recommending unnecessary feeding.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining Rubber Plant leaf drop. Cover natural ageing, recent moves, moisture and roots, temperature, draughts, light and pests, with a pattern-based inspection sequence. Avoid attributing every dropped leaf to overwatering or promising recovery.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining Fiddle Leaf Fig leaf drop. Cover leaf position, recent changes, moisture and roots, light, temperature, draughts and pests, and explain when isolated loss differs from continuing decline. Avoid single-cause diagnosis and rigid schedules.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining a drooping Calathea. Cover daily leaf movement, moisture, roots, temperature, humidity, light and recent disturbance, helping readers distinguish temporary posture from sustained loss of firmness. Avoid assuming thirst from drooping alone.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining brown ZZ Plant leaf tips. Cover physical damage, moisture history, roots and rhizomes, salts or feeding, heat, cold and natural ageing. Avoid diagnosing from tips alone, recommending fixed flushing routines or promising reversal.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining stretched, leaning or weak Aloe vera growth. Cover light direction and intensity, rotation, watering, temperature, pot stability and the limits of correcting existing growth. Avoid telling readers to move plants abruptly into harsh sun.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining Phalaenopsis orchid bud drop. Cover environmental change, temperature, draughts, moisture and roots, light, humidity and ethylene exposure where supported. Avoid certainty from one symptom and guarantees that unopened buds can be saved.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to choosing pot size for houseplants. Explain root-ball fit, drainage, stability, plant habit, cachepots and why oversized containers can complicate moisture management. Avoid universal size increments, arbitrary annual upsizing and product promotion.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining bottom watering for houseplants, when it can be useful, its limitations, safe technique and how it fits with drainage and occasional top watering. Avoid presenting it as universally superior or giving fixed soaking times for every plant.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to white fungal growth on houseplant compost. Cover how to distinguish surface fungal growth from mineral deposits and pests, conditions that favour it, proportionate moisture and ventilation changes, and when root or crown symptoms require closer inspection. Avoid unnecessary fungicides.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining when to leave, trim or remove damaged houseplant leaves. Cover remaining green tissue, disease uncertainty, clean tools, pet or child safety, plant size and recovery priorities. Avoid claiming pruning cures underlying care problems.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to watering houseplants after repotting. Explain how plant type, root disturbance, fresh medium, container drainage and season affect the decision, and how to reassess moisture safely. Avoid one universal immediate-watering rule or fixed waiting periods.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining why drainage holes matter for houseplant moisture management, how nursery pots and cachepots can work together, and the risks of planting directly into sealed containers. Avoid promising that drainage layers substitute for an outlet.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to using tap water for houseplants. Cover regional variation, sensitive plants, visible deposits, water temperature, practical alternatives and when changing water is unlikely to solve the real issue. Avoid blanket claims about chlorine, fluoride or leaving water overnight.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to assessing whether a houseplant needs more light. Cover stretched growth, smaller leaves, slowed growth, leaning, variegation changes and seasonal context, while distinguishing light issues from root, moisture or temperature problems. Avoid universal lux thresholds.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to recognising and responding to sunburn or leaf scorch on houseplants. Cover symptom position, recent moves, window exposure, heat and acclimatisation, with safe relocation and monitoring steps. Avoid diagnosing every pale or brown patch as sunburn.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to heat stress in houseplants during warm weather. Cover leaf temperature, direct sun, drying rate, roots, ventilation and watering assessment, with practical stabilisation steps. Avoid fixed temperature cut-offs for all species and reflexive overwatering.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to moving home with houseplants. Cover preparation, safe packing, temperature exposure, legal and practical transport limits, unpacking, pest inspection and gradual placement. Avoid guarantees against damage and unnecessary immediate repotting.

Prepare an evidence-led UK winter houseplant care guide. Cover reduced light, slower drying, heating, cold windows, draughts, feeding decisions and pest monitoring, while emphasising plant-by-plant assessment. Avoid universal winter watering calendars or blanket dormancy claims.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to yellow leaves on Monstera. Cover leaf age and position, moisture history, roots, light, temperature, nutrition and pests, with a practical inspection order that distinguishes one ageing leaf from a continuing pattern. Avoid diagnosing overwatering from colour alone or promising damaged leaves will recover.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining sideways, leaning or uneven Monstera growth. Cover light direction, the plant's climbing habit, support, rotation, container stability, aerial roots and the limits of reshaping established stems. Avoid abrupt relocation into intense sun, forced bending or guarantees of symmetrical growth.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining slow or absent visible growth in Pothos. Cover seasonal growth, light, temperature, moisture and roots, recent repotting, pruning and realistic recovery expectations. Distinguish stable slow growth from decline and avoid unnecessary feeding, automatic repotting or rigid growth-rate claims.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to brown spots on Peace Lily leaves. Cover spot position and development, physical damage, moisture and roots, direct sun or heat, cold, pests and possible disease indicators. Explain when monitoring is appropriate and when isolation or removal is reasonable, without diagnosing from photographs or recommending routine fungicide use.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining curled Peace Lily leaves. Cover moisture consistency, roots, light and heat, temperature changes, humidity, pests and emerging leaves, with a symptom-led inspection sequence. Avoid assuming thirst from curl alone, prescribing fixed watering intervals or promising existing leaves will flatten.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining slow or absent visible growth in Calathea. Cover season, light, temperature, moisture and roots, humidity, water quality where relevant, recent repotting and pests. Help readers distinguish slow stable growth from decline, avoiding fixed growth targets, unnecessary feeding and automatic repotting.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to brown Snake Plant leaf tips. Cover physical damage, moisture history, roots and rhizomes, salts or feeding, heat, cold and natural ageing. Distinguish dry tip damage from spreading soft tissue or discrete leaf spots, and avoid diagnosis from tips alone, fixed flushing routines or promises of reversal.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining slow or absent visible growth in Rubber Plants. Cover seasonal growth, light, temperature, moisture and roots, recent moves or repotting, pests and realistic expectations. Distinguish stable slow growth from active decline and avoid unnecessary feeding, automatic pot changes or rigid growth-rate claims.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide to curling Fiddle Leaf Fig leaves. Cover leaf age, moisture and roots, light and heat, temperature changes, humidity, pests and mechanical damage, with a practical inspection sequence. Avoid assigning one cause from curl direction alone or promising established leaves will return to their previous shape.

Prepare an evidence-led UK guide explaining Phalaenopsis orchid roots growing outside the pot. Cover normal aerial roots, healthy and unhealthy root appearance, ventilation, moisture, potting medium, container condition and when repotting is or is not warranted. Avoid telling readers to cut healthy aerial roots, force them into the pot or repot solely because roots are visible.
